subject: Clarify SOC 2 coverage for split-month ownership change and point-in-time evidence
messages:
From: Ana Lopez <security@acme-corp.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendes <carlos.m@acme-corp.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SOC 2 Type II: question about split-month coverage and point-in-time evidence

Hi Jordan,

Quick question on the SOC 2 Type II you provided: Acme completed an acquisition on 2026-10-18 and we need to confirm whether your report (covering Oct 1–Oct 31) can be relied on for the portion of the month post-acquisition. Specifically:

- Do you consider a report that includes a point-in-time snapshot (logs, config exports) taken on 2026-10-15 as covering controls for the whole month of October, or only up to that snapshot?
- If not, would a bridge letter be provided to clarify continuity of controls across the ownership change?

We're coordinating internally with our auditors; any confirmation or suggested language would help.

Thanks,
Ana Lopez
Security Manager, Acme Corp
(415) 555-0123

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Ana Lopez <security@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II: question about split-month coverage and point-in-time evidence

Hi Ana — thanks for the clear context. Short answer: the Type II report's period is Oct 1–Oct 31 inclusive, but how a point-in-time snapshot is treated depends on the control objective.

High level:
- For design/implementation evidence (policies, configs), a point-in-time export can often be used to demonstrate the control as of that instant, but auditors usually prefer continuous evidence for operating effectiveness.
- For log-based controls, a snapshot mid-month doesn't prove coverage for subsequent days unless paired with retention/forwarding controls showing continuity.

We can:
1) Share the delivered Type II (PDF) for your auditors to review (attached).
2) Draft a bridge letter that clarifies the acquisition date and which controls were continuous vs. limited to the pre-acquisition entity.

Marissa (our audit lead) is looping in — she can propose wording and confirm what evidence we can supply (e.g., config exports, log retention statements).

Would you prefer a short, auditor-ready bridge letter or a more detailed narrative for your internal team?

Best,
Jordan Blake
Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
Attachments: SOC2_TypeII_20261031.pdf (pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ana Lopez <security@acme-corp.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II: question about split-month coverage and point-in-time evidence

Hi Ana — Jordan summarized it well. A few concrete points from an audit perspective: 

- The SOC 2 Type II report covers Oct 1–Oct 31. That read is what external auditors cite. A point-in-time artifact dated Oct 15 documents the state on that day only.
- Common approaches we see that are acceptable to auditors:
  * A bridge letter that explicitly notes the acquisition on Oct 18 and confirms which control activities and personnel were unchanged.
  * Supplementary evidence that demonstrates continuity (e.g., centralized log forwarding config, retained logs spanning Oct 15–Oct 31, or access-control change logs).

I've attached a bridge letter draft with suggested language and two optional paragraphs you can include about log retention and custody. If you want, we can:
1) Finalize the draft with specific timestamps (UTC) and the acquisition legal docs you provide.
2) Produce a short evidence pack (log extract + config export) — we can redact sensitive fields.

A couple of quick clarifying Qs for your team:
- Do you need the bridge letter to state controls are effective for the entire month, or just to clarify which controls were continuous?
- Can you share the exact legal transfer timestamp (date/time) you have on record?

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Audit & Compliance Lead
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Bridge_Letter_Draft_20261127.docx (docx)

From: Ana Lopez <security@acme-corp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II: question about split-month coverage and point-in-time evidence

Thanks Marissa — helpful. A few answers:

- For external reporting to our board and for our auditors, we need explicit language that says which controls they can rely on for the post-acquisition period (Oct 18–Oct 31). Saying "continuous where noted" is not sufficient for the audit report.
- The legal transfer effective timestamp is 2026-10-18T14:30:00Z (we'll provide the transfer doc).

Action items for Redwood to confirm:
- Can you confirm whether you can state that administrative access provisioning and centralized logging remained under Redwood control across the transfer?
- If you provide a bridge letter, please include UTC timestamps and an exhibit listing the log ranges or evidence file names.

If you can produce the bridge letter with exhibit references, we'll forward to our auditor and let you know if they request additional evidence.

Best,
Ana

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Ana Lopez <security@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2026 16:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II: question about split-month coverage and point-in-time evidence

Ana — thanks for the timestamp. Confirming next steps we will deliver: 

1) Finalized bridge letter (auditor-ready) that:
   - References the Oct 1–Oct 31 report period, the Oct 18T14:30:00Z transfer timestamp, and which controls are continuous.
   - Includes an exhibit listing evidence artifacts (we'll reference log extracts and config export filenames).

2) Evidence pack: a log extract spanning 2026-10-14T00:00:00Z through 2026-10-31T23:59:59Z (CSV stub attached), plus a config export showing centralized logging and provisioning settings.

3) We will use UTC timestamps and can redact sensitive fields in the exhibit.

I'll attach the draft bridge letter and the SOC 2 PDF; Marissa will finalize language for the continuous controls statements. Expect the first draft by EOD tomorrow.

Best regards,
Jordan Blake
Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
